outcome: maternal outcomes (pulmonary edema, pleural effusion, serum albumin levels)
cohort: The study included 721 women with singleton pregnancies diagnosed with preeclampsia after 20 gestational weeks, who delivered at >=22 gestational weeks, and had results from a spot urine protein/creatinine ratio test at delivery.
finding: Severe proteinuria significantly increased the frequency of preterm delivery and was associated with a higher frequency of maternal pulmonary edema/pleural effusion, especially in women with nonsevere hypertension, with hypoalbuminemia being a key factor.
gest_age: >=20 gestational weeks at diagnosis of preeclampsia; >=22 gestational weeks at delivery
